$schema_note: Week-1 retrieval gold set (60 questions) for wiki/designs/agentm-rescope-week1-experiment.md. Scored with the P@5/R@5 code in scripts/health/eval_v6_retrieval.py against both arms (FTS5-only vs FTS5+vector). Entry shape: {id, question, expected_note_paths, stratum, source}. `expected_note_paths` are vault-relative, resolved against plugins.obsidian-vault.vault_path — never hardcode the absolute path.

$strata.distinctive-token: 12 — question shares an uncommon term (proper noun, package name, slug) with the target. Mined from real prompts in ~/.claude/projects/ transcripts.
$strata.pure-paraphrase: 18 — question shares no content word with the target's text. Operator writes these cold; placeholders below.
$strata.episodic-temporal: 12 — question references when or in what context something happened. Operator writes these cold; placeholders below.
$strata.research-density: 10 — question targets ONE note inside a dense near-identical cluster under projects/agentm/research/*/reference/. Precision, not recall.
$strata.negative: 8 — the true answer is 'no such memory exists.' Verified absent across the entire vault including personal/_inbox/ and the retirement-listed directories.

$labeling_constraints.no_fragments: No expected_note_path points at a miner fragment — a body opening 'User stated:' / 'Fix observed:' / 'User corrected the agent:', or a mid-word slug under personal/idea/ or personal/fix/. 3,393 of the vault's 8,588 markdown files are that shape and are not valid ground truth even when they contain the fact.
$labeling_constraints.no_retired_files: No expected_note_path points at anything on the retirement list in wiki/designs/agentm-rescope-memory.md: personal/_opinions/, personal/_watchlist/, personal/_skill-watchlist/, _meta/skill-discovery-cache/, _idea-incubator/, _moc/, _meta/ health-scorecard + forward-learning + orchestration state.
$labeling_constraints.question_provenance: distinctive-token questions are transcript-sourced. Where a mid-session prompt did not stand alone (a bare 'yes, do that'), the operator's information need and its distinctive token are preserved and the session-only referent is dropped; the wording is otherwise his.
$labeling_constraints.paraphrase_bar: The design's literal bar — 'shares no content word with the target note's text' — is unmeetable on a technical vault: a question about worktrees that avoids the word 'worktree' is a riddle, not something anyone types. Operational bar, ratified 2026-08-06: no RARE collision, where rare means the shared term appears in under 2% of the 4,475 eligible notes. A term above that (design 17.9%, agentm 21.3%) is ambient vocabulary and gives lexical ranking no handle. Every paraphrase entry records its sharpest collision below.

$deferred.question: Why did AgentM never fully realize the vault vision that I had, forcing me to do a second re-write when we got to FRIDAY?
$deferred.why_deferred: The answer is a repo file, not vault content, so no arm can retrieve it from the 8,030-file week-1 corpus. Both arms would fail equally — the A/B comparison survives, but the slot measures nothing. The vault holds only partial answers: F1-REAUDIT.md states the as-built capture path contradicts the designed one, and progress-r0-engine-repairs.md carries the inbox-backlog finding. Neither is the diagnosis being asked for.
$deferred.activation_condition: Promote into `entries` once the rescope designs live under desk/projects/ per the layout in agentm-rescope-memory.md. This is the mirror of the retirement-list rule: that rule stops the set labeling against files about to disappear; this stops it discarding questions whose targets have not arrived yet.
$deferred.superseded_for_week_1_by: pp07 — the same question narrowed by deletion to the half the current vault can answer. Promoting this one later does not retire pp07; they ask at different altitudes.
$deferred.clause_note: The original ended '...but actuall didn't?'. Operator dropped the clause 2026-08-06 as unresolvable rather than pick a reading; whoever promotes this decides what a right answer looks like.

entries.question: In the built-in ranker, can we change how quickly repeated occurrences of a term stop adding to a document's score, or is the per-field boost the only lever we get?

If we need to find a fragment sitting in the middle of a longer string rather than a whole word or a prefix, which indexing choice supports that — and does the same index also speed up ordinary pattern-match queries?

One of the ways the server can collapse a model's output isn't usable for similarity search at all — it hands back a single number instead of anything you can compare with cosine. Which one, and what endpoint needs it?

One of the two candidate embedding models only wants the instruction sentence glued onto the thing being searched with, never onto what we index, and barely suffers if we skip it entirely. Which model, and what is the exact sentence?

Our watch on a single file goes dead after the first save. What does the library do to its own bookkeeping when a path gets renamed, and why isn't simply re-registering the watch afterwards enough to close the hole?
Can we rely on getting a modification notification for a directory itself when something inside it appears or disappears, or does that depend on which platform we're running on?
What's the reported hazard of pointing the repository-open call at a directory that turns out not to be a repository at all — does it just error out cleanly?
If we take the library's stock diff settings, how alike do two files have to be before it calls the pair a rename, and is there a ceiling on how many pairs it will compare looking for one?
Why does the compiler keep bundled assets uncompressed inside the executable when squeezing them would obviously make it smaller — what capability would compressing them have broken?
If the build-time value injection points at a symbol path that no longer exists after a package gets moved, do we find out at build time, or does the binary just ship with the wrong value?
What did we settle on for backing the vault up to Backblaze B2 — bucket layout and retention?
Show me recent research you've ingested on current security vulnerability trends as it pretains to my current homelab setup and my github projects.
entries.note: personal/domains/security/ looks populated but holds only scaffolding — threat-model.md is a triage lens with no findings, the four stack-*.md files are scan targets captured 2026-06-03, trusted-security-sources.md is the whitelist the unbuilt V7-6 vuln-watch sidecar would fetch from. No advisory has ever been ingested. The whole vault contains four CVE identifiers: three in _idea-incubator/ (retiring) and one in a design doc. A lexical arm should surface threat-model.md and stack-agentm.md with high confidence, and be wrong.
